Drama
Intent
Our curriculum will inspire students to develop the creative and personal skills in a variety of disciplines whilst building and developing vital life skills such as confidence, team work, empathy, independence, appreciation, co-operation, creativity, communication, critical thinking and resilience.
The Drama Department want to nurture students' theatrical ability through a diverse array of activities aimed at enhancing their acting talent. Our professional approach includes lessons that are focused on the exploration of voice, body, and performance skills, adopting an understanding that enables students to enhance their confidence in a safe space. By allowing the students to refining their presentation skills, students are empowered to apply them in their future careers.
Impact
Our curriculum is created to meet the students' needs, providing a secure and controlled environment for exploring issue-based drama. Through this, students are encouraged to make sense of their own experiences, fostering the development of expressive and interpersonal skills. The subjects and concepts covered in Drama contribute to enriching and shaping students' experiences, aiding in the formation of their values, attitudes, and life philosophy. Moreover, students actively engage in practical exploration of various issues, enhancing their confidence and self-esteem.
Implementation
Throughout Key Stage 3 the students are taught key skills in drama, to enhance pupils’ creativity to broaden their understanding, appreciation and application of a wide variety of different drama styles, once a week.
In addition to classroom work, pupils are encouraged to take part in extra-curricular music activity, such as the school plays, drama club and show case nights.
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
During Year 7 the foundations of drama skills are explored, students come to secondary with a mixture of experience on the stage mostly from their end of school productions. The students explore these drama skills through practical lessons, exploring different themes and topics which allow them to have a good understanding of how to work well in a group, develop their social skills as well as performance skills alongside having the ability to critically evaluate their own work and overcome creative difficulties.
Year 8
In Year 8 the students will start to hone their skills on the stage and we will cover topics that allow the students to explore modern day issues, explore texts that reflect the journey to GCSE drama and allowing the students to use performance skills to develop interesting and creative performances. By the end of Year 8 students will be confident in the skill of performance that will allow them to have a passion for the subject.
In Year 9, students build upon their passion for the subject, refining their skills and creating dramatic and powerful performances. In Year 9, we explore the history of theatre, exploring styles ranging from ancient Greek drama to Surrealism. Students also study influential theatre Practitioners and various theatrical styles, gaining a deeper understanding of the art form. They channel their creativity by devising an original play tailored for younger audiences through Theatre in Education. Finally, we take an exciting trip to the theatre to experience a live performance and evaluate it critically, evaluating the acting skills and theatre technology that goes into a Live Performance.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
We follow OCR Drama GCSE because it has:
A practical approach to assessment – There’s a high percentage of practical assessment in the non-examined assessment and a single portfolio assessment for students.
There are three components:
Devising Drama Component: 01 Students will create their own devised performance based on a chosen stimulus from the exam board stimulus paper. In addition to the performance, students will be marked on an accompanying portfolio with evidence of the process and decisions made whilst creating and developing their performance.
Presenting and Performing Texts Component: 02 Students will take part in a showcase, demonstrating their chosen skills in a live performance. Students will perform in or design for two performances from one text. Students will be required to produce an accompanying document which outlines their intentions for and approach to the performance showcase.
Drama: Performance and Response Component: 03 This component requires students to study text and performance. For Section A, students study one performance text in detail from a set list given by the exam board. This section of the paper will contain questions which require short and medium length answers. It assesses students’ knowledge and understanding of how drama is developed and performed. In Section B, students will be required to analyse and evaluate a live theatre performance they have seen using accurate subject-specific terminology.
KS5 (Years 12 & 13)
BTEC National Level 3 Performing Arts Acting:
Students will work on the premise that they are their own theatre company and build their performance skills through working together and performing to live audiences.
Students will take part in a number of live performances to a chosen audience both in the Drama studio and the main hall.

Art & Design, fashion
The Art Department is made up of two Art teachers. We pride ourselves on having very high expectations and providing an exciting and innovative learning environment.
The schemes of work aim to challenge and inspire all learners in Art. We constantly review and improve our projects to ensure that pupils are engaged, learn new skills and develop independence and creative thinking.
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will inspire students to develop knowledge of the world around them through personal investigations into a broad range of traditional and contemporary artists, designers, craftspeople and cultures. They will develop their knowledge, understanding and skills of two and three dimensional materials through a wide range of creative, exciting and stimulating learning experiences. Our teaching and learning will ensure students are encouraged to look at artworks and the world around them, to consider why objects, artefacts and things we take for granted look the way they do; to appreciate that everything we use in life has been designed by someone with an artistic eye or artistic background.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure all students achieve mastery whilst cultivating their artistic skills. They will become proficient in working safely with a wide range of equipment, including photography, and computer-aided design using industry software Adobe Creative suite , whilst manipulating and combining various materials. They will also develop their investigative skills through critical analysis tasks and regular pieces of extended analytical writing. In addition, they will expand their experience through a range of extracurricular gallery and museums visits, as we help them mature into our future artists, designers and craftspeople of the future.
Implementation
The Art curriculum encourages creative curiosity, independent learning and develops critical and analytical individuals who are ready to express themselves, using themes that interest them.
Students will be given the opportunity to experience working in a wide variety of 2D and 3D media and materials. Teachers will provide opportunities for writing and reading in the form of artist analysis. All written work will be marked in line with the school’s literacy policy. Great emphasis is placed on sketchbook use to present development and organise visual information.
To develop knowledge and understanding of art, reviewing, adapting and refining their work, sketchbooks will be used to encourage students to feel a sense of ownership of their work, and to provide opportunities for extended research, homework and development of presentation skills.
Year 7 learn basic art skills, which underpin the knowledge, skills and understanding, needed to explore art and to make progress in the subject.
In Year 8, students can develop these skills through more challenging projects.
The aim of Year 9 is for pupils to apply their skills and understanding to the sustainable development of an idea.
Students develop the capacity for creative thought and action; the ability to innovate, initiate and make effective personal responses needed in GCSE art. Leading to KS4 and beyond, students have the opportunity to be inspired by art in galleries and museums on our art trips.
Teachers will connect and weave learning and skills holistically across all strands by implementing our bespoke scheme of work.
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
Year 7
Introducing the formal elements.
Students will analyse the artwork of a variety of artists and will learn how they effectively used colour theory.
Observational drawing is an integral component of art. Often, drawing is the core method of researching, investigating, developing and communicating ideas.
Colour is one of the fundamental elements of art. It is important for art students to not only be exposed to colour theory, but to understand it.
Year 8
Building on observational drawing skills and understanding the use of colour and pattern in more depth.
Studying the work of other cultures and craftspeople to understand symbols and traditional cultural influences.
Introducing new techniques, experimenting with new media and working with card or clay to form 3D sculptures.
Year 9
Pupils in Year 9 who opt to take Art will complete a diverse range of workshops centered around three projects (one per term).
Students will have five lessons over the two week timetable and will build up an extensive skill-set working in media from sculpture to printmaking to textiles and fine art.
Term 1 - Natural Forms and Still life.
Term 2 – Everyday objects – Food and Drinks: 3D Sculpture project
Term 3 – Exploring other cultures.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
Year 10/11 GCSE ART
Students will take an independent approach to their GCSE project and devise a topic to investigate.
In Year 10, students will begin their investigations looking at influences from a range of artists who are specific to the project theme, and then eventually link this to their own interests. This theme will be explored and developed using a wide range of skills and techniques reflecting the style of both contemporary and historic artist links. The pupils will produce an exciting and original portfolio of work that reflects the four assessment objectives.
KS5 (Years 12 & 13)
A Level
Students in Year 12 will begin a project based upon the theme of Surface and Texture which will lead to an independent investigation into artists of choice and development work.
In Year 13, students choose their area of focus for the Contextual Study and produce work relating to that theme.
KS5 Curriculum Maps and other useful resources - click here
Fashion and Textiles Course
Students who choose this course as an option at A level will study a range of different techniques and processes to cover the following disciplines.
Students will design and create their own fashion and clothing collections that will be showcased in an end of year exhibition and Fashion Show.
Critical and contextual studies in fashion.
Fashion and Textiles techniques and processes.
Fashion visualisation and presentation.
Pattern cutting techniques and processes.
Draping on the stand.
Hand and machine sewing techniques and processes.
Garment manufacturing processes.
Clubs
We run an Art Club after school.
We welcome all students to the club and enjoy having a range of ages working together. Students also have the opportunity to attend catch up session's afterschool on Mondays.
Art Exhibition
We hold an annual Art Exhibition of GCSE and A Level work in the summer term.
This is a fantastic opportunity to celebrate the achievements of our Art students.
Rewards & Competitions
We run various competitions throughout the year, both internal and external, to maintain the level of challenge for our learners including our annual Christmas Card Competition.

English
Our department of highly enthusiastic, motivating teachers help and guide every student to develop their love of English Language and Literature during their time at Highcrest and enable them to flourish in this subject, preparing them for a range of future courses and job positions.
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will inspire our students to appreciate the power of language and the opportunities that it provides for success in an ever-changing society and empower them to develop curiosity, imagination, expression, empathy and tolerance. Through our inspirational teaching we will build their confidence, creating literate, independent thinkers who are empathetic and go on to become life-long learners. The English Curriculum is founded on a shared love of language and literature, and within our department, we endeavour to explore a variety of themes and ideas that are universal and relevant to today. Our students will fully understand that English is at the very heart of every aspect of learning and shapes our understanding of human experience. Through our text choices students will develop their capacity to understand and empathise with the endless worlds around and within them.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure that the key skills and information needed at GCSE level is taught from Year 7 (at a Key Stage 3 level) as this will deepen knowledge and understanding of a variety of skills, texts and historical contexts. We will expand students’ knowledge and understanding by building on skills learned in previous years and ensuring that they learn how to become more critical and analytical as they progress through their education. We will also expand their knowledge further through relevant trips, visiting companies and real-life experience that links to their studies and key texts.
The English department are driven through a passion for reading and writing. We are dedicated to ensuring this is the foundation of our curriculum and this passion is seen in our classrooms each and every day. We endeavour to ensure children across the school read carefully and accurately, with empathy and understanding. We champion creativity and a love of creative writing.
Our five year curriculum plan aims to build on the foundations laid during KS2. Our KS3 schemes of work serve as a ‘springboard’ to prepare students for the three year GCSE course and ensure that they have the skills required to access the topics relevant to their aspirational targets.
Implementation
Our curriculum scales in the difficulty of texts, depth of knowledge and complexity of ideas from entry in Year 7 up to our A-Level Literature course. Each scheme of learning focuses on specific and transferable knowledge linked to the texts and genres studied. We teach writing through reading, providing high quality examples from literature to evidence techniques and skills a writer uses in their craft.
In Year 7 students study a curriculum based on the theme of ‘Storytelling’: starting from studying the origins and history of ancient tales, the use of fable and allegory in Animal Farm, the gothic genre and ‘The Tempest’ as Shakespeare’s final story.
Year 8 is based on the theme of ‘The Power of Words’: students study the Oliver Twist & Pygmalion scheme of learning, exploring ideas of poverty, class and gender in Victorian England and how this is represented in literature. Students study contemporary poetry and how modern issues are reflected in poetic form, and they also study the dystopian genre and Shakespeare’s ‘Romeo and Juliet’.
In Year 9, students develop ideas about ‘The Writer’s Craft’ as they build on upon their contextual and analytical essay writing skills, exploring all areas of a text for meaning and effect through Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, and encouraging alternative viewpoints and nuances of life experience in Victorian Women. They study the Voices for Change scheme of learning exploring how great speakers, poets and thinkers have used their words to change the world we live in, the ‘Power and Conflict’ poetry anthology, and a range of fiction and non-fiction extracts.
In Year 10 and 11 students focus on developing their reading and writing skills through both English Language and English Literature AQA GCSE courses. We focus on ensuring students retrieve key knowledge through regular retrieval tasks, develop the rigour and depth of their thinking through discussion, extended writing opportunities and annotation. Read a variety of diverse, high quality text choices across the world of literature in their Language course and develop confident understanding of the plot, structure, language, methods and ideas of the GCSE texts: An Inspector Calls, A Christmas Carol, Romeo and Juliet and the Power and Conflict Anthology.
Our A-Level English Literature course runs through Year 12 and 13 building on the foundation of ideas from KS3 and 4, developing opportunities for wider reading, critical analysis through a range of literary criticism of the texts studied, encouraging independent reading and exploration of ideas, depth of discussion and a love of literature!
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
Students study a range of exciting topics in KS3 with an equal focus on Reading and Writing skills where they are encouraged to develop ideas, argue their point of view and explore the ideas and contextual factors behind given texts. Pupils will be encouraged to read, act and create their own pieces of writing around a variety of topics and ideas.

Geography
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will inspire students to understand what it is to be a geographer. They will be able to carry out increasingly complex, independent geographical enquiries, ask their own relevant questions, make sense of geographical data, think critically about different views, and justify their own views in reaching conclusions. Our teaching will ensure students have a holistic understanding and an extensive bank of geographical knowledge and vocabulary, which will be learned and practiced regularly so that students are confident and comfortable using academic language in every context that requires it throughout their education and beyond.
We have a strong Geographical element of the Humanities department, with three subject specialists and a number of others supporting the delivery lessons who have strong foundation in Geographical knowledge.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure all geographers will have an appreciation for the world they live in and a deeper understanding of how their actions can have an impact on the people and places around them. Students will have a drive and passion for finding out about the world and its people, as well as having a keen interest and inspiration to travel, in order to deepen their knowledge and understanding. Indeed, we enrich our curriculum through a range of field trips, visits and other extracurricular activities, including The Duke of Edinburgh Award, that all contribute to students developing strong independent learning skills, both within and outside of the classroom, and becoming critical and analytical learners. We foster enthusiasm for our discipline and subsequently prepare our students for further education and potentially careers in related fields.
Implementation
Within Geography we deliver lessons of high quality and foster engagement and a curiosity of learning. Each lesson will be highlighted with clear intentions linked to prior skills/knowledge and future learning. Pupils will be taught Geographical concepts and begin to consider their importance in the development of the world over time, they will delve into studying elements of physical and human elements of Geography in detail. Assessments are meaningful and continuous using detailed analysis to promote constant individual learning opportunities. We will assess pupils' memory retention and in specific subject specific exam techniques, teaching them the structures needed to achieve success. The curriculum is continuously quality assured, monitored and improved upon as a collaborative team. Additional interventions are provided to all students with different focuses picked up and identifies through continuous assessment throughout the topics.
In Year 7, pupils will study an introduction to geographical skills. This allows us to assess their knowledge gained at primary and ensure they have a good foundation ready to begin the Geography study. This unit involves learning about grid references, continents, contour lines and an introduction to fieldwork. Pupils then move on to to undertake in-depth studies into; Rivers, Techtonics, Development, Ecosystems and then a case study on Japan where they will apply all their knowledge learned this year.
In Year 8, pupils begin to delve into the wider world looking at the concepts of globalisation and industries. They consider the costal landscapes and impact of climate change, weather and climate, looking at how it affects our world. Pupils will do an in-depth study into deserts and revisit their study of geographical skills to ensure that they are secure and confident in these.
In Year 9, pupils begin to be given a taste of GCSE study and look beyond the UK at three key elements of Biomas, Hazards and resources across the globe. This will allow pupils to take a more thematic approach to their studies and gives pupils the opportunity to begin to look at areas of geographic study which overlap in their impact.
In Years 10 and 11, pupils studying Geography will undertake the AQA GCSE Geography full course studying both Physical and Human units to give them a wide breadth of understanding of the global issues and challenges across the world today.
At A Level, pupils move onto looking at in-depth studies of key geographical elements both Physical and Human and will begin to investigate their own areas of interest through their NEA study; this is their opportunity to showcase their understanding.
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
Across Key Stage 3, pupils study a variety of both Physical and Human units to begins to introduce them to the two areas of geographical study. They learn the foundation of geographical skills they will need for future study and learn how to incorporate it into the topics they are learning.

KS5 (Year 12 & 13)
In Key Stage 5, pupils will be taught in subject areas allowing the staff to focus on their own specialities, giving pupils the in-depth knowledge they need to achieve their grades.

The Importance of Field Trips
Outdoor learning and experiencing the environment being taught is an integral aspect to Geography here at Highcrest.
With that in mind, students are offered a huge variety of field trips. The opportunities run throughout the Key Stages, have included local trips to High Wycombe, London, Wendover Woods and Lulworth Cove. We also have many trips further afield to Epping Forest, London, Majorca, Italy and Iceland and Naples, some have occurred in recent years and others are coming up.

Computer Science/ICT
Welcome to Computer Science.
Our department brings together dedicated and knowledgeable teachers who pair strong academic expertise in Computer Science with extensive real-world experience in the tech industry, both in the UK and internationally. This unique combination of technical knowledge and practical insight ensures that students gain a deep understanding of core computing principles while also exploring how these ideas are applied in modern technological environments.
We are committed to equipping students with the skills, creativity, and confidence needed to succeed in today’s fast‑moving digital world. Through interactive lessons, hands-on coding activities, collaborative projects, and real-world problem-solving, students develop a solid foundation in programming, cybersecurity, networking, artificial intelligence, web development, and computational thinking.
Intent
Our challenging curriculum will inspire students to develop their knowledge and understanding of Computer Science through studying the role of computing in the world today and how it will evolve in the future. Through practical involvement in a range of activities, students will apply their knowledge and develop skills to help them succeed in the subject. Our teaching and learning will help students develop a real applied focus to coding, independent thinking and problem-solving. Students will also understand how technology can be used to tackle current world issues. They will develop valuable transferable skills and have the exciting opportunity to progress to the next level of study in this subject.
Impact
Our curriculum has been developed to ensure that all our students have the opportunity to gain knowledge and understanding of the subject through a variety of project-based learning tasks. Students are encouraged to work independently, for example to solve logic problems, but still support each other when required, as this develops well rounded and confident young people. This is a popular subject, which has proved, over recent years, how in demand computer science skills are and how vital technology is to the growth of the economy. This is a popular subject, which has shown, over recent years how in demand computer science skills are and how vital technology is to the growth of the economy.
Implementation
Staff in our department are committed to:
Our Computer Science and ICT curriculum is designed to equip young people with the ability to use technological tools to find, explore, analyse, exchange, and present information in a variety of contexts. The effective use of ICT also enhances the learning power of students by developing their creative and thinking skills, collaboration and independent learning.
Computer Science and ICT gives students essential skills for life and enables learners to participate and contribute in a rapidly changing world.
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
In the lower school (KS3), ICT/Computer Science is taught through Years 7 and 8 on a carousel with Technology subjects. In their ICT lessons pupils will cover topics which include: an introduction to algorithms and basic programming, using Python, binary coding and how computers can be useful to us in the 21st and beyond. The modules of work also include modelling using spreadsheets, multi-media and data handling, and pupils will use a variety of theory and practical resources.
In Year 9 pupils can choose to follow either a Computer Science skills-based course or an Introduction to iMedia course. These courses are designed to provide an insight into our exciting yet challenging GCSE courses and will help further develop their skills in the areas of programming languages, hardware, applications software, digital media creation and cyber security. These foundation courses provide our students with a range of transferable skills which will enable them to be successful in other curriculum areas, and in future education or employment.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
In Year 10 pupils will have selected their GCSE level qualifications and work starts in earnest. We offer a choice of GCSE Computer Science and OCR Cambridge Nationals iMedia L1/2. Both these qualifications have a practical element, whether that be using Python programming language in GCSE Computer Science or designing and creating digital graphic products in OCR iMedia.
KS5 (Years 12 & 13)
Currently we offer both Level 2 and Level 3 BTEC IT/Computer Science related qualifications in our Sixth Form. ICT courses at KS5 are both challenging and demanding, and students will need to be fully committed to completing work at home and after school in order to achieve at the highest level.

Business
Welcome to Business.
Our department brings together experienced teachers who combine strong academic expertise in the field of Business with extensive real-world experience across a wide range of industries in the UK and internationally. This blend of knowledge and practical insight ensures that students benefit from both theoretical understanding and authentic business perspectives.
We are committed to equipping students with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to succeed in today’s dynamic global economy. Through engaging lessons, collaborative projects and real-world case studies, students build a solid foundation in entrepreneurship, finance, marketing, management, and economics.
Intent
The intent of the Business curriculum is to equip students with the foundation of knowledge of key topics such as Entrepreneurship, Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Operations and Leadership. They will learn how contemporary issues (e.g. Covid, the war in Ukraine and the cost of living crisis) impact the business environment. Students will be encouraged, from an early stage, to develop their analytical and evaluative skills so that they are able to construct well-balanced arguments backed up by sound evidence (and therefore achieve the top grades). Above all, the intent is to develop students into enterprising individuals who have the ability to think commercially and creatively so that they are able to solve business problems, make informed business decisions and are well equipped to progress on a variety of career paths.
Impact
The success of the curriculum will be largely measured by the results achieved in OCR and GCSE Business (Key Stage 4) and A-Level and BTEC Business (Key Stage 5), together with the numbers of students who continue to study Business (or related subjects such as Marketing, Entrepreneurship, Accounting or Finance) in Higher Education. However, we also judge success by levels of participation in enterprise activities around the Academy, such as the Young Enterprise Programme in Sixth Form, and by how well students emerge from their study of Business able to discuss confidently changes in the economy, society and technology and how they affect businesses.
Implementation
Within Business, we strive for high quality, inclusive teaching that engages all students in the class. Each lesson will start with clearly defined learning objectives, linked to prior knowledge and learning, so that students are clear on expectations of them. We strive for a range of blended learning opportunities, with plenty of scope for students to work independently, either individually or in groups. High levels of interaction are the cornerstone of our lessons, with constant dialogue and questioning about events in the real world and how they impact on businesses. We review and quality assure our resources regularly to ensure that they are up to date with the ever-changing world of business. We also teach students about effective exam technique, so that they can construct appropriate responses to different command word questions e.g. ‘explain’, ‘analyse’ or ‘justify’; this is critical to achieve exam success.
KS3 (Year 9)
Students in Year 9 follow a programme of study which has been developed by teachers at the Highcrest Academy to enthuse pupils about the world of business. Students will enjoy a range of projects each focused on a key building block of Business. Competing in an entrepreneurship ‘Dragons’ Den’, they will showcase their amazing business ideas and plans. Students will experiment with different marketing methods, such as designing webpages and writing blogs. Applying the fundamentals of finance to their own personal finances, they will learn effective budgeting, saving, investing (in the stock market) and managing cash flow. Participating in ‘mock’ job applications and interviews will build their understanding of human resources. A range of operations challenges will test their ability to produce the highest quality product with the optimal resources. Finally, through a range of group projects and presentation, they will unleash their own leadership potential.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
We offer two qualifications in KS4:
An outline is each is shown below.
Edexcel GCSE Business is examined by two exams in the summer of Year 11, each of which is 1 hour 45 minutes long. Each paper is a mix of multiple-choice, short-answer and extended-writing questions using case studies. The content of the course is as follows.
Year 10: Theme 1 - Investigating small business. This theme comprises five topic areas relating to new and small businesses.
Year 11: Theme 2 - Building a business. This theme’s five topic areas focus on larger and well- known businesses, using case studies such as Tesco, Apple and BMW.
OCR Enterprise & Marketing
This qualification has three mandatory units:
Unit R067: Enterprise and Marketing Concepts (exam). In this unit, you will learn about the key factors to consider and activities that need to happen to operate a successful small start-up business. Topics include:
Unit R068: Design a Business Proposal (coursework). In this unit, you will identify a customer profile for a specific product, complete market research to generate product design ideas, and use financial calculations to propose a pricing strategy and determine the viability of their product proposal. Topics include:
Unit R069: Market and Pitch a Business Proposal (coursework). In this unit, you will develop pitching skills to be able to pitch your business proposal to an external audience. Finally, you will review your pitching skills and business proposal using self-assessment and feedback gathered. Topics include:
Edexcel GCSE Business
OCR Enterprise & Marketing.

KS5 (Years 12 & 13)
We offer two alternative qualifications at Level 3:
AQA A Level Business - students learn ten topics over the two years, covering the core functional areas of Business (management/leadership, finance, operations, marketing and human resources) and extensive coverage of the different strategic challenges facing businesses in the modern era and the options available to them. Assessment is by three exam papers at the end of year 13.
BTEC National Diploma in Business – this is worth two A levels and involves eight units over the two years. In Year 12, students study: Exploring Business, Developing a Marketing Campaign, Personal & Business Finance and Recruitment & Selection. In Year 13, they study Managing an Event, International Business, Principles of Management and Training & Development. Three of these units are exam/controlled assessments and the other five are coursework.
We also offer the BTEC First Certificate in Business, which is a Level 2 qualification available to relevant students. This qualification, consisting of eight units over one year, covers: Enterprise in the Business World, Finance for Business, Promoting a Brand, Principles of Customer Service, Recruitment, Selection & Employment, Principles of Marketing, Using Business Documentation and Financial Planning & Forecasting.

construction
Intent
Our Construction and the Built Environment curriculum will inspire students to design and fabricate construction jobs to help solve real-life problems. Our teaching facilities are complemented by our exceptionally well-equipped workshop, which contains both manual and electronic machine tools used in the construction industry. These are used to develop students’ Construction knowledge, skills and understanding, whilst opening their minds and developing their imagination and creativity skills. We will give our students the opportunities to expand their horizons and build meaningful learning outcomes connected to the real life, in readiness for a future career.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure all students develop both the practical skills and theoretical knowledge needed to solve design briefs. Our curriculum will ensure students gain skills in becoming tradesmen. They will deepen their knowledge and understanding enabling them to make critical and analytical judgements of construction problems and products. They will expand their experience of construction through a range of trade skills and build upon previous knowledge to support overall pupil development. In addition, we prepare our students for the many opportunities a career within Construction can offer and build skills which are transferable across the world of work such as; literacy, numeracy and mathematics, estimating quantities, choosing the right materials, problem-solving and evaluation.
Implementation
The WJEC Level 1/2 Vocational Awards (Technical Awards) provides learners with the opportunity to study vocational subjects alongside GCSEs and alongside other general vocational qualifications as part of a broad programme of study.
At Highcrest, the Construction lessons target learners in KS4, who find it difficult to focus and develop in normal classroom settings. Construction offers an experience that focusses on applied learning and development of problem-solving and hypothetical techniques. The two-year course offers both technical knowledge as well as practical skills on a 40% academia to 60% practical weighting.
The Construction Award provides the learner with opportunities to progress into either a college setting or an apprenticeship scheme. At The Highcrest Academy we have made local connections in Buckinghamshire College through our on-site professional careers advisors.
KS4 (Year 10 & 11)
Led by experienced professionals, our construction qualification at The Highcrest Academy is designed to give learners the skills that will prepare them for employment. So, whether it's learning construction drawing techniques or learning about the use of science and mathematics in construction, the skills and knowledge students will pick up in this Construction and Built Environment course will help learners to achieve success in the construction industry.
This innovative Level 1/2 qualification was developed in partnership with CITB and is primarily designed for learners aged 14-16 who want to learn about the construction industry from the build perspective. It provides learners with a broad introduction to the different trades involved in the sector and the range of career opportunities available.

Creative imedia
Intent
The intent of the Creative iMedia curriculum is to develop students’ knowledge, understanding and practical skills that would be used in the media industry. Specifically, students will be able to apply their creative iMedia learning to practical, real-life situations, such as developing visual identities for clients, together with creating original digital graphics and original digital media products. We will aspire and provide opportunities for students to achieve and expand their creativity in digital graphics in preparation for their future career pathways and the digital media world.
Impact
The success of the curriculum will be largely measured by the results of students achieved in the qualification. For this qualification, students must achieve three units: one externally assessed and two Non Examined Assessment (NEA) units. Students undertake the following units and assessment methods:
The impact will also be measured by the success of students in advancing into Level 2 and Level 3 vocational qualifications including those in Digital Media and Information Technology, A Levels, T Levels or apprenticeships; these will all open doors to creative career paths in the future.
Implementation
Within our department, we strive for high quality, inclusive teaching that engages all students in the class. Each lesson will start with clearly defined learning objectives, linked to prior knowledge and learning, so that students are clear on expectations of them. The focus of the classes is highly practical, with students applying their knowledge to different scenarios, such as to develop visual identities for clients and use the concepts of graphic design to create original digital graphics to engage target audiences. They will undertake the whole life cycle with regards to interactive digital media, from planning to creating and then reviewing the digital media.
Our Creative iMedia curriculum is designed to equip young people with the ability to use technological tools to find, explore, analyse, exchange, and present information in a variety of contexts. The effective use of ICT also enhances the learning power of students by developing their creative and thinking skills, collaboration and independent learning.
Creative iMedia is a dynamic and engaging subject that equips students with essential 21st-century skills, fostering creativity, critical thinking, and digital literacy. Through a hands-on, project-based approach, students develop a comprehensive understanding of media production, from concept development to final output.
KS3 (Years 7, 8 & 9)
In the lower school (KS3), ICT/Computer Science/iMedia is taught through Years 7 and 8 on a carousel with Technology subjects. In their ICT lessons pupils will cover topics which include: an introduction to algorithms and basic programming, using Python, binary coding and how computers can be useful to us in the 21st and beyond. The modules of work also include modelling using spreadsheets, multi-media and data handling, and pupils will use a variety of theory and practical resources.
In Year 9 pupils can choose to follow an Introduction to iMedia course. This course is designed to provide an insight into our exciting yet challenging KS4 course and will help further develop their skills in the area of understanding how to use appropriate software and tools to create a digital end product. They will research digital graphics and discover how they are used in the media and entertainment industry. These foundation courses provide our students with a range of transferable skills which will enable them to be successful in other curriculum areas, and in future education or employment.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
In Year 10 pupils will have selected their GCSE level qualifications and work starts in earnest. OCR Cambridge Nationals iMedia L1/2 offers a creative alternative to GCSE Computer Science. This qualification has a very practical element, as pupils will be taught the many stages and processes involved with the design and creation of digital graphic products, but in a very structured and measured way.
KS5 (Years 12 & 13)
Currently we offer both Level 2 and Level 3 BTEC IT/Computer Science related qualifications in our Sixth Form. ICT courses at KS5 are both challenging and demanding, and students will need to be fully committed to completing work at home and after school in order to achieve at the highest level.

Design Technology
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will inspire students to understand that Design and Technology is intrinsic in our lives and must not be something we take for granted. Our teaching and learning will inspire learners to draw on skills and knowledge acquired in Maths, Science and Art, helping them become innovative and enhance the world around them by creating solutions to real problems. We will ensure that students recognise that the products that we use every day have been meticulously designed to intuitively make even the most mundane tasks seem easy and comfortable, and that this doesn’t happen by accident. We have a wide range of subjects for students to study within the department which include:
Construction (Years 10 - 11)
Engineering (Years 10 - 11)
Food Technology (Years 7-11)
Resistant Materials (Years 7-11)
Textiles (Years 7-11)
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure students comprehend and are able to utilise all aspects of the design process, both with their DT lessons, and in other curriculum areas. They will develop a true understanding of how to work from concept to completion; making analytical and justified use of research as they transform their initial thoughts into working three dimensional outcomes. They will become proficient in working safely with a wide range of tools, equipment and machinery, whilst manipulating and combining various traditional and smart materials. In addition, they will expand their experience through a range of extracurricular visits and opportunities that will support our taught curriculum. We will inspire them to be our next generation of engineers, designers or craftsman who are interested in following a career path in engineering, design or nutrition.
Implementation
Design Technology students will undertake part practical and part theory courses covering a range of skills in research through investigation, designing, planning and making and elements of Computer Aided Design (CAD). They will gather essential life skills and be encouraged to think about our environment. The units taught have been specifically designed to give the students a hands-on experience and can prepare them for a career in the very wide Technology industry.
At KS4 the units have practical and theoretical elements with students requiring to produce evidence in the form of practical making projects of their choosing according to the challenges set by the exam board. Each element of the units is graded according to the exam board's criteria and mark scheme levels 1-9. Each student is encouraged to keep track of their process to enable their progress.
The aim of the courses in Design Technology are to give students experience, knowledge and skills working with workshop tools, machinery and equipment that will enable them to be creative, problem solve and enjoy a range of design applications which would help them to either make career choices or provides the learner with opportunities to progress into a college setting as well as grow into rounded individuals.

Engineering
Intent
Our Engineering curriculum will inspire students to design and manufacture innovative products to help solve real-world problems. Our teaching facilities are complemented by our exceptionally well-equipped workshop, which contains both manual and CNC (Computer Numerical Control) subtractive and additive manufacture machine tools. These are used to develop students’ engineering knowledge, skills and understanding, whilst opening their minds and developing their imagination and creativity skills. We will give our students the opportunities to expand their horizons and build meaningful learning outcomes connected to the real world, in readiness for a future career.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure all students develop both the practical skills and theoretical knowledge needed to solve design briefs. Our curriculum will ensure students gain skills in becoming engineers, designers or craftsman. They will deepen their knowledge and understanding enabling them to make critical and analytical judgements of engineering problems and products. They will expand their experience of engineering through a range of extra-curricular visits that include trips to a range of manufacturing facilities and design-based museums. We will prepare our students for the many opportunities a career within engineering can offer and build skills which are transferable across the world of work.

All students are provided with weekly Engineering lesson. Through the KS4 curriculum, students develop skills in all areas of the design process. It is a subject that is inspiring, rigorous and practical, preparing all young people to value the world they live and work in, one that considers sustainable designing and making. They are taught to consider real problems and how the interactive design process can help them in analysing, researching, designing, modelling, developing and evaluating possible solutions to problems – whilst also developing independent learning, as well as group work. Throughout the course, students will be challenged with a range of designing and making tasks that use a variety of techniques, materials and processes, as well as a range of materials, tools and equipment including CAD and CAM. In addition to this, Engineering students are given frequent opportunities to discuss wider issues, such as technological development, sustainability and responsibilities of designers and manufacturers. Engineering is a subject that we believe is a life skill – relevant to whatever the students do later in life.
KS3 (Year 9)
All students are provided with a weekly Engineering lesson. The students will develop skills in all areas of the design process. They are taught to consider real problems and how the interactive design process can help them in analysing, researching, designing, modelling, developing and evaluating possible solutions to problems – whilst also developing independent learning as well as group work. Students will be challenged with a range of designing and making tasks that use a variety of techniques, materials and processes, as well as a range of materials, tools and equipment including CAD and CAM.

They will continue to undertake projects in which they research, design, make, analyse and evaluate their progress as well as understand the relevant equipment, tools and materials needed. They gather information, make choices and reflect on how technology affects society. Students are given the opportunity to think and intervene creatively to improve the quality of life. Engineering is a subject that we believe is a life skill.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
The Qualification in Engineering Design
At The Highcrest Academy students have the opportunity to study the OCR Cambridge National in Engineering Design (J822).
Engineering Design is a process used to develop and enhance new products and systems as a response to market opportunities.
This qualification, taken over two years, challenging both academically and in the workshop, gives students an insight into what it is like to work in the engineering design and development industry. Students learn how to use both 2D and 3D engineering drawing techniques to communicate design ideas and how to design new products to meet a design brief.
Students have the opportunity to develop their hands-on practical skills in the workshop, such as metal work, 3D printing, using smart materials, to compliment their academic work.
The qualification has three units and is assessed using both an exam assessment and two non-exam assessments (NEAs).
R038 Principles of engineering design
In this unit students learn about the different stages involved in the design process. They learn about different designing requirements and how to communicate design outcomes and evaluate design ideas. Exam assessed.
R039 Communicating designs
In this unit students learn how to communicate design ideas using a range of techniques, including manual production of freehand sketches and engineering drawings, as well as using computer aided design (CAD). Centre assessed.
R040 Design evaluation and modelling
In this unit students will learn how to model design ideas and test them as well as how to evaluate products. Centre assessed.

Our Courses & options
The Highcrest Academy Sixth Form is made up from approximately 170 students divided into mixed Year 12 and 13 tutor groups.
We offer a wide range of Level 2 and 3 courses and the timetable is constructed around the choices made by individual students, ensuring all students can study their preferred combination of subjects.
The majority of our current Year 11 students are expected to continue into the Sixth Form; however, we do welcome applications for Year 12 from external students.
We pride ourselves on excellent, small group teaching and one-to-one support when required, whilst every student is viewed as an individual with individual needs. A great deal of time and effort is invested to ensure that each student is settled and able to work effectively.
In Year 12, students study either three or four Level 3 courses (either BTEC L3 or A Level) or two Level 2 courses. Students can mix A Level and BTEC courses depending on their future career aspirations. We also offer students who wish to improve their GCSE Maths and English grades the opportunity to re-sit these qualifications throughout their time in Sixth Form; any student who achieved a grade 3 or below in their GCSE Maths or English must re-sit this course during Year 12. In Year 13, students will traditionally go down to three courses, although some have taken four, where appropriate.

Welcome to Child Development. This course is designed for students with a passion for working with children.
This course will allow you to progress on to further study within this sector or seek employment within the child-care sector. The mandatory content of the qualification incorporates topics relevant across the childcare sector.
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will support learners’ understanding of the developmental norms of children from birth to five years, as well as the stages and benefits of play. Our teaching and learning will ensure students gain a real insight into all of the challenges, excitement, considerations and responsibility surrounding children’s development and the number of agencies and people involved in caring for that development. This course aims to challenge students to investigate the equipment needed for babies, toddlers and preschool children up to five. The Child Development course encourages multiple approaches to learning, such as practical opportunities and real-life scenarios, which will support students to develop their applied knowledge and practical skills.
Impact
Our curriculum is designed to ensure that all students are fully engaged in their learning and play an active role in every lesson. Through high-quality, knowledge-rich teaching that combines both theoretical and practical elements, alongside purposeful home learning tasks, students will develop strong independent learning skills both in and beyond the classroom. Students will become confident, critical, and analytical learners, equipped to make informed decisions in the planning, completion and evaluation of their NEA coursework, as well as in demonstrating their understanding successfully in examinations. We aim to foster a genuine enthusiasm for the subject and, in doing so, prepare students for future study and careers in related fields such as Child Care, Health and Social Care, Psychology, Sociology and Biology.

NCFE CACHE LEVEL 2 TECHNICAL AWARD IN CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND CARE

OUR EAL provision
Catering for a variety of learners, the EAL department offers support to students with varying levels of proficiency in the English Language, aiding in accessibility and promoting achievement and independence.
Our EAL Provision at The Highcrest Academy
The EAL (English as an Additional Language) department at The Highcrest Academy provides tailored support for students at varying levels of English proficiency. Our goal is to ensure every student can fully participate in lessons, achieve their potential and develop independence and confidence in English.
Our Aim
We aim to enable our EAL students to fully engage with all areas of the curriculum by:
Supporting students to become confident, independent learners
Building confidence in the mainstream classroom environment
Our Students
The Highcrest Academy is proud to have a vibrant bilingual and multilingual student community. Some students are recent arrivals to the UK, while others have been living here for several years. Across the school, approximately 23% of students speak English as an additional language, and around 42 different languages are spoken at home, reflecting the wide range of cultural and ethnic backgrounds within our school.
EAL students are integrated into mainstream lessons with structured support from our specialist LSA, who provide personalised English intervention and assist with learning in all subjects. With tailored guidance and encouragement, we aim for all EAL students to make progress in line with their peers.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive and welcoming environment where every student can thrive academically, socially and personally, celebrating the rich diversity of our school community.
Celebrating Multiculturalism
We value the rich cultural diversity of our student body and celebrate the variety of languages spoken within the school. We:
Promote appreciation of all cultures and languages
Celebrate International Mother Tongue Day
Foster strong social connections across cultural groups
In-Class Support
EAL LSAs work alongside subject teachers to help students succeed in mainstream lessons. Support may include:
We also integrate technology to support language learning, with iPads available to assist with translation, definitions and independent research.
Clarifying teacher instructions
Assisting with reading, writing and comprehension
EAL Interventions
Students identified for additional support work with our EAL LSA in dedicated intervention sessions. These focus on developing:
Interventions are tailored to students’ individual needs, ensuring they can engage fully with all subjects.
Vocabulary and grammar
Spoken and written fluency

Bedrock Vocabulary Programme
All KS3 students, along with selected KS4 EAL students, use the Bedrock vocabulary programme to strengthen their English skills. The programme is accessible both at school and at home, allowing students to practise independently and at their own pace.
Students are encouraged to earn a minimum of 20 points per week, with higher point totals leading to faster progress. This gamified approach motivates students, helping them expand their vocabulary, improve comprehension, and develop stronger writing and literacy skills more quickly.

Literacy is central to learning at The Highcrest Academy. EAL students benefit from:
These initiatives, alongside focused support, enable all students to make consistent progress in using English confidently in everyday and academic contexts.

HAIR & BEAUTY
Welcome to Hair and Beauty, these courses are suitable for people with a passion for hair or beauty. As a certified VTCT centre offering both the level 1/2 Technical Award in the hair and beauty sector and a level 2 Certificate in Beauty Services; we pride ourselves on offering the most up-to-date courses that will benefit our students. Our hair and beauty courses have been designed to offer students an insight into one of the world's biggest industries. With both theoretical and practical elements, students will gain a thorough understanding of what it takes to be a professional individual and work in the hair and beauty industry. This course will allow them to progress onto further study or seek employment within this sector.
Intent
Our knowledge-rich curriculum will support learners’ understanding of the field of hair and beauty for both KS4 and KS5, as well as the biological makeup of the human body. This course aims to challenge students to investigate the equipment needed to facilitate hair and beauty treatments, as well as the personal considerations of carrying them out. The hair and beauty course encourages multiple approaches to learning, such as practical opportunities and real-life scenarios, which will support students to develop their applied knowledge and practical skills. In KS4 the students will explore the world of business relating to hair and beauty, the history of the industry from ancient times to present and product formation. Our KS5 curriculum is much more focused on preparing the students for industry, with a large emphasis of the course looking into client care, health and safety and how to adapt treatments to meet clients needs.
Impact
Our curriculum will ensure all students are fully engaged in their lessons and play an active role in their learning. Indeed, our project-based schemes, portfolio approach and home learning plan will contribute to them developing very strong independent learning skills, both within and outside of the classroom, and becoming critical and analytical learners, able to make decisions. We will foster enthusiasm for the discipline and subsequently prepare students for careers within this pathway.
Implementation
Hair and Beauty students undertake a mainly practical course covering a range of hair and beauty units, listed below. These units have been specifically chosen to give the students a better insight in to the hair and beauty industry and guide them towards the part of the sector they enjoy most.
All units have a practical and theoretical element with all requiring portfolio evidence in the form of practical assessments, assignments and some requiring further evidence such as mood boards. Each unit is graded individually and will be given a grade of pass, merit or distinction based on VTCT's criteria. This course is certificated and will detail the grade of each unit on it.
The aim of this course is to give students a real insight into what working within the industry would be like and allow them to leave with a certificate and start work as soon as they are able or willing to.
KS4 (Years 10 & 11)
CO2A5 VTCT Level 1/2 Technical Award in the Study of Hair and Beauty
Throughout Years 10 and 11 the students will work on their course which is mainly theoretical. During this time the students will learn about the history of the hair and beauty industry, cosmetic sciences, anatomy and physiology and business studies relating to the sector. We also implement fortnightly intervention sessions that focus on the practical abilities of students and allow us to improve their current working at level and increase their ability to attain a higher level. The full units the students will undertake are listed below.
There are regular assessments throughout Year 10 and unit checks to ensure students have a full understanding and abundance of knowledge surrounding the unit they have covered. In Year 11, the students will undergo their mock exams, coursework and final written exam. Theses are all graded as below with the coursework grade accounting for 60% of the overall grade:
Weekly intervention/revision sessions are offered to all students, especially those requiring extra support to improve students' knowledge and overall grade. The aim of this course is to develop students' understanding of how a business is set up and run, the costs involved and the effects of the products used in these businesses on the hair and body. Reporting Student Absence
“It is important to be here every day to receive a good education. Teachers want us to learn, they push us and say to try our best. If you are not here, you miss also socially because you do not see your friends.” Year 10 Student, speaking with the Inclusion Quality Mark Assessor
Please call 01494 529866 and press 1 for our attendance line or email attendance@highcrestacademy.org.uk.
Is my child well enough to go to school today?
FACT: Research shows that prior to the pandemic in 2019, secondary school students who did not achieve grade 9 to 4 in English and Maths missed on average 10 more days during their GCSE courses than those who achieved grade 9 to 5 in both English and Maths.
We understand that sometimes children are genuinely ill and of course you must be the judge of this. However, it is vital that we work together to prevent your child having odd days of absence – or “avoidable absence” linked to coughs, colds and mild anxiety. At Highcrest we expect parents to play a full and responsible part in ensuring that their child attends school regularly and is on time in the morning.
The following our guidelines from the NHS and Department for Education: to help you decide whether your child is well enough to attend school.
Your child should attend school, even with the following…
To help your child through the day, give your child a dose of paracetamol before school, and send them into school with plenty to drink. Let Matron know if you are concerned about your child in the morning.
Sore throat, tonsillitis and glandular fever.
Head lice.
Conjunctivitis.
Your child may need to take limited time off school with the following…
*Please let Matron know, as pregnant members of staff may be affected.
If you believe there are other factors which are causing reluctance to come to school, please contact your child’s Head of Learning. You can find our useful contacts list here.
Please call 01494 529866 and press 1 for our attendance line or email attendance@highcrestacademy.org.uk.
Why attendance counts..
When is my child allowed to miss school?
FACT: The higher a pupil’s attendance, the more they are likely to learn, and the better they are likely to perform in exams and formal assessments.
There are only a small number of circumstances where missing a school day is permitted. Your child must attend every day the school is open, unless:
What should I do if my child needs to be absent from school?
FACT: Parents and carers have a legal duty to ensure their child gets a full-time education.
Where can I get support to help my child attend school?
FACT: At Highcrest, we are here to help and support you improve your child’s attendance.
FACT: Being in school is important to your child’s achievement, wellbeing, wider development and mental health.

Personalised Interventions
Some students may require a more personalised approach to their learning. We offer a small range of targeted interventions designed to address identified barriers and close gaps both academically and socially. Our experienced Learning Support Assistants work with students in and out of the classroom, providing tailored support that helps them develop key skills, confidence, and independence. Some students may require a more specialised intervention, and this may be delivered by an external agency.
Literacy and Numeracy Support
Learning Support Assistants are trained to deliver Precision Teaching. A dedicated literacy and numeracy intervention to track and monitor progress whilst helping consolidate learning and close the gap in these areas. Students requiring this intervention will have daily intervention. This ensures the skills learnt are accurately applied. Students see success daily and are more motivated to engage in learning.
To support a small number of learners who have been identified as struggling readers, we use Ruth Miskin’s Fresh Start, a proven systematic phonics programme. Learners are carefully screened to identify specific barriers to reading, and where appropriate, they take part in daily targeted interventions to address identified gaps. Fresh Start accelerates reading accuracy, fluency, and stamina. The intervention is delivered by two trained Learning Support Assistants, ensuring consistency and high-quality support.
Social Skills
Some students require help managing their interactions and ability to communicate with peers and adults. Learning Support Assistants run social skills groups following the Talk About for Teens programme. Sessions are held weekly for identified students. We also have a fully qualified Emotional Literacy Support Assistant, ELSA, who holds 1:1 intervention for students requiring a more targeted approach to managing their emotional regulation.
Key Steps Curriculum and ASDAN
A small minority of students are disapplied from Modern Foreign Languages and will instead complete the ASDAN awards; Key Steps and Personal Development Programme. Key steps take place in Year 7. In Year 8 we follow ASDAN’s Personal Development Programme. A student disapplication is decided by the SENDCo working in collaboration with parents, Assistant Heads of Learning, Heads of Learning, department staff and other professionals already supporting the student. A combination of information from KS2 attainment, initial assessments undertaken upon entry to The Highcrest Academy and the specific learning needs of each student are considered on a case-by-case basis before a final decision is made.
In Key Stage 4 a small cohort of students may opt to work towards the ASDAN course Personal Social Development at either Entry Level 3 or Level 1.
If a student is identified as requiring SEN Support families will be informed. Provision will vary according to the needs of the individual student. This may be in the form of in class support from Learning Support Assistants, in house intervention run by Learning Support Assistants or Higher-Level Teaching Assistants. Some students may be in receipt of intervention run by external agencies.
Forest School Group
For some of our more vulnerable learners we offer the opportunity to experience Forest School. Forest School at The Highcrest Academy has a holistic, inclusive, proactive and learner led approach to education in natural environments. We build confidence, resilience and friendships together through small achievable tasks. We work with the Chiltern Rangers, in small groups in the school and with the wider community . We are eco champions for our setting and our natural surroundings. Our Forest School participants will develop skills they already have and learn how to adapt to situations. In a safe and secure environment, we will learn how to assess and take risks. Through working together with new materials, tools, peers, habitats and ways of thinking, Forest School participants and practitioners will achieve and support each other. Through a planned programme on a 6-week cycle with identified students, we will have weekly sessions where we will assess and monitor our achievements through work-based activities. Once a term we will have a whole day excursion to support volunteers in our local community to protect our woodlands, streams and wildlife. Forest School is a safe environment, but most of all Forest School is fun!
Miss A Watson, Forest School Practitioner
Examination Support
Some students may require Access Arrangements and or reasonable adjustments for external examinations. Access arrangements allow candidates with specific needs, such as special educational needs, disabilities or temporary injuries to access an examination and show what they can do without changing the demands of the assessment. The Highcrest Academy must follow the clear guidance regulation of JCQ (Joint Council for Qualifications). Please see the Exam Policy for specific details.
